findings.F1: The test ran on all four folds, so no more data is available, and its 10-day slope sits at zero (t 0.29 on 445 negative-forecast cells). The same cells in folds B and C at 10 days give slope t 0.22 (215 cells), and the depth quartiles of the calm stretch are not ordered: excess 10-day returns of -1.7 %, -6.2 %, -4.4 % and -1.2 % from the deepest to the shallowest quartile (about 46 cases each).
findings.F2: On the same negative-forecast cells the graded effect shows at shorter horizons. The slope of the drift-removed return on the forecast has t 2.67 at 3 days (738 cases) and t 2.58 at 5 days (435 cases), against 1.96 at 7 days and 0.22 at 10 days.
findings.F3: At 5 days the gain comes from the deepest stretches. The deepest quartile of the forecast (mean -18.2) is followed by an excess return of -3.3 %, the next quartile by -1.3 %, and the two shallower quartiles by +0.2 % and -0.6 %.
findings.F4: At 3 days the short side's drift-removed gain is +1.0 % per case (t 2.19 with the cases of one day together, 258 days). The slope is positive on all six coins (t from 0.25 to 1.78), so the short-horizon effect is not carried by one coin.
findings.F5: The effect is mixed across years, and this is likely why the 10-day result is drowned. At 3 days the short side's excess is +2.5 % in 2018 (t 2.65) and +1.0 % in 2019 (t 1.66), but -1.1 % in 2020 and -0.9 % in 2021. The calm 10-day slope swings from t +1.98 in 2020 to t -5.02 in 2021.
findings.F6: The agitated side behaves differently from the calm side at 10 days. Calm cells below the average have a mean drift-removed return of -3.4 % (t -3.38, 183 cases), while agitated cells have +0.2 % (t 0.17, 172 cases). The calm-market fall is therefore real on average, but it is not graded by depth at 10 days.

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the further a coin's close sits below its 20-day average, measured in units of the standard deviation of its daily returns over the same 20 days, the more it keeps falling, over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a calm market shorts a deep stretch below the average for days rather than for two weeks, because the graded follow-through fades before ten days.
ideas.name: calm stretch falls five days
